Jonas —

Appreciate the heads up and the file. High-level guidance: we should avoid being locked into a single home-court forum that increases enforcement risk for Redwood in regulated indemnity/enforcement scenarios. That said, we also want to be pragmatic on medium-size commercial deals. Proposed approach (pick one to present):

Option A (preferred for enterprise): Mutual interim relief carve + neutral forum for disputes.
- Add express language preserving either party's right to seek injunctive or other provisional remedies in any competent court notwithstanding arbitration.
- Keep arbitration for merits, but require venue for injunctive relief to be governed by the court where the party seeking relief files (mutual).

Option B (middle ground): California law, but split venue and emergency relief.
- Governing law: California.
- Venue for actions at law and enforcement: Santa Clara County.
- Injunctive relief: emergency/provisional relief allowed in any court of competent jurisdiction (mutual).

Option C (deal-sweetener): Redwood accepts site jurisdiction for small-dollar deals (<$100k ARR) but retains neutral venue for larger commitments.

Aditya — can you draft specific short clause options (one paragraph each) we can send to Ellen with rationale (enforceability + speed)? If you think arbitration carve should remain explicit, note how we preserve remedies without opening broad self-help.

Ellen — sharing options to keep this moving; happy to discuss over a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

All —

Drafted three succinct clause alternatives below that track Kim's options. Copying them into the thread so Ellen/Michael can mark a preference; I formatted them to drop straight into the Word redline.

Option A (Enterprise / Redwood preferred) — Mutual provisional remedies exception
"Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or protect its confidential information or intellectual property; the seeking of such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right of either party to have disputes finally resolved by arbitration under this Agreement."

Rationale: preserves arbitration for merits while ensuring quick access to courts for emergency relief and clear IP protection.

Option B (California law + neutral injunctive carve)
"This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The parties agree that any action at law or for enforcement of a judgment shall be brought in the state or federal courts located in Santa Clara County, California. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction as necessary to preserve the status quo or protect its rights pending resolution by arbitration."

Rationale: meets their ask on California law/venue but preserves mutual right to injunctive relief anywhere.

Option C (Deal-specific carve)
"For Orders with Annual Recurring Revenue less than $100,000, Redwood consents to exclusive venue in the state and federal courts of Santa Clara County, California for all actions. For Orders equal to or greater than $100,000, the parties shall use Option A above. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional remedies in any court of competent jurisdiction."

Rationale: gives commercial leverage on larger deals while accommodating procurement-approved small deals.

Next steps: I can drop any chosen option into the Word doc and send a clean redline. Jonas — if Stratus pushes back on Option A, Option B is a fast compromise. Ellen — please indicate preference and we can aim to finalize language today.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Associate General Counsel
